root.note: Latin studium comes from studēre, ‘to be eager’.

history: Studio first meant ‘eagerness’. Latin studium was the zeal with which a person pursues something, from the verb studere, ‘to be keen’. Learning is something you do with zeal, so the word moved to ‘study’. Italian studio kept both the action, lo studio della matematica, and the place where work is done with application: the room of a scholar, then a painter's atelier, then the office of a professional. So a doctor, a lawyer or an accountant has a studio medico, studio legale or studio commercialista, and you make an appointment there. English study, student and studio all come from this root, the last borrowed from Italian in the 1800s. Italian studente and studiare are in the same family.
historyEinfach: Studio comes from Latin studium, ‘eagerness’. It means study, and also the office of a doctor, lawyer or accountant (studio medico, studio legale). English study, student and studio are relatives.

elsewhere.text: English borrowed studio from Italian in the 1800s for an artist's workshop, and later for a place where films and music are recorded.
